title: The behavior of red foxes
body: Red foxes are solitary hunters that pounce on rodents hidden under snow. Their orange coat and white-tipped tail make them easy to recognise at the forest edge at dusk.

title: Vulpes vulpes in the modern city
body: Vulpes vulpes is among the most adaptable wild fox species on Earth. Urban populations now den under sheds and forage in parks, living alongside people with surprising ease.

title: How gray wolf packs work
body: A gray wolf pack is usually a family group led by a breeding pair. Pack members cooperate to hunt large prey like elk and travel long distances across their territory.

title: Why Canis lupus howls
body: Canis lupus howls to rally the pack, mark territory and locate separated members. A howl can carry for kilometres across open tundra and forest.

title: Caring for your family dog
body: Pet dogs need daily walks, a consistent feeding routine and regular vet check-ups. Positive reinforcement training keeps a household dog calm and happy.

title: Brown bears and the salmon run
body: Every autumn, brown bears gather at rivers to catch migrating salmon. The fat they build now carries them through the long winter.

title: Inside Ursus arctos hibernation
body: Grizzlies and other Ursus arctos populations den for months, lowering heart rate and body temperature. Mothers even give birth during this winter sleep.

title: How deer grow antlers
body: Male deer grow a new set of antlers every year. Covered in velvet while growing, the antlers harden before the autumn rut and are shed in late winter.

title: Cervids during the autumn rut
body: During the rut, stags and bucks spar with their antlers and call loudly through misty woodland to attract mates.

title: Emperor penguins survive the Antarctic winter
body: Emperor penguins huddle in tight groups to survive temperatures far below freezing while males incubate eggs on their feet.

title: What makes a coral reef healthy
body: Healthy reefs depend on clear water, stable temperatures and a balance of fish that graze algae off the coral.

title: Keeping a sourdough starter alive
body: Feed your starter flour and water on a regular schedule and keep it at a steady room temperature for a lively, bubbly culture.
